items.stimulus: The conservator placed a vase from a nineteenth-century expedition on a padded shelf that had been damaged during transport. The museum loaned the portrait to the university after it had restored the frame. Researchers examined a meteorite in the laboratory that contained unusual crystals. The curator interviewed the cartographer about a map who had worked in the region for decades. <u>Because the labels were written in pencil, the archivist stored</u> the maps in acid-free folders. These careful procedures help museums preserve objects while making them available for study.

items.stem: Which is the best version of the underlined portion?
choices: a map in its central gallery, that Marín had drawn
in its central gallery that Marín had drawn a map
in its central gallery a map that Marín had drawn
items.stimulus: In 1912, the city of Fairhaven hired surveyor Elena Marín to chart the coastline around its harbor. Marín and her assistants marked shoreline elevations with brass instruments and copied the measurements into notebooks. The museum displayed <u>a map that Marín had drawn in its central gallery</u>. Marín stored the notebooks after she had cataloged the measurements in a locked cabinet. The museum’s curator found that Marín had drawn the northern inlet twice while examining the completed map.
items.explanation: Placing “in its central gallery” immediately after “displayed” clearly identifies the gallery as the location of the display, not the location where Marín drew the map.

per_choice.correct: Placing “in its central gallery” immediately after “displayed” clearly identifies the gallery as the location of the display, not the location where Marín drew the map.
